chunks: Al-Sadiq عليه السلام offered condolences to a man for his son, and he عليه السلام said to him: “Allah is better for your son than you are, and the reward of Allah is better for you than him.”
Then his intense grief after that reached him, so he returned to him and said to him: “The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله has died; do you not have in him an example?”

He said to him: “He was approaching maturity.” So he said to him: “Indeed, ahead of him are three qualities: the testimony that there is no god but Allah, the mercy of Allah, and the intercession of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله. Not one of them will escape him, if Allah, Mighty and Majestic, wills.”

key_terms.أُسْوَةٌ: an example or model to follow
key_terms.رَحْمَةَ ٱللَّهِ: Allah’s mercy granted to the deceased
key_terms.شَفَاعَةَ رَسُولِ ٱللَّهِ: the intercession of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.عَزَّى: offered condolences and comfort after a loss

ai.seo_question: How did Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام console a parent grieving the death of a child?
ai.summary: This hadith records Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام consoling a grieving father by redirecting him toward trust in Allah and hope in divine reward. When the father continued in grief over his young son, the Imam reminded him of the death of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and reassured him of Allah’s mercy, shahadah, and the Prophet’s intercession for the child.
